# CLI reference

Every command takes `--config PATH` (`-c`); without it, flib reads `$FLIB_CONFIG` or `~/.config/file-librarian/config.yaml`. `flib --version` prints the version, and `flib COMMAND --help` shows what this page shows.

*This page is generated from the command line itself (`uv run python -m scripts.docs_cli`), so it cannot drift from it.*

## flib init

Set flib up step by step, then try it on copies of your recent files.

Nothing in your folders moves: the trial runs on copies in a temporary folder, with a throwaway index. With --local, nothing leaves this Mac: it checks that Ollama is installed and running (it never installs it), offers to download the recommended models, and says what quality to expect.

```text
flib init [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Accept every default without asking. |
| `--force` | flag |  | Replace an existing configuration without asking. |
| `--sample` | integer | `30` | Recent items to try it on; 0 skips the trial. |
| `--local` | flag |  | Keep everything on this Mac: a local model through Ollama, local text recognition and local semantic search. |

More: [Getting started](getting-started.md#first-run-flib-init).

## flib key

Store an API key in the macOS Keychain (anthropic, openai-compat, embeddings).

```text

```

More: [Providers](providers.md#anthropic-anthropic-the-default).


### flib key set

Save the API key in the Keychain (asked for, never shown).

```text

```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider` | text |  | anthropic, openai-compat, or embeddings (semantic search's server) (default: the configured provider, else anthropic). |

```text

```


| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider` | text |  | anthropic, openai-compat, or embeddings (semantic search's server) (default: the configured provider, else anthropic). |

## flib status

Show what waits for you: files in review and why, failures, the last and next run.

Also files left in place as sensitive and this month's provider cost. It only reads: no lock, nothing created, and it works before the first run. ``--sensitive`` lists those files by path, here only: never in `flib doctor`, a notification or the MCP server.

```text
flib status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print JSON. |
| `--sensitive` | flag |  | List each file left in place as sensitive, and why (names!). |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#what-waits-for-you).


## flib search

Find organized files by name, description or tags, and by category, period or type.

Without a query, the files matching the filters are listed newest first. With --semantic, files are also found by meaning ("invoice" finds a "bill"), if close enough (search.semantic.min_similarity); --no-semantic turns it off for one search when search.semantic.default is true. Duplicates are left out unless --duplicates is given. --issuer, --kind, --min-amount/--max-amount, --currency, --due-before/--due-after and --period filter by what the AI read in the document. --sum adds up the amounts of every match instead (never mixing currencies), --by groups them; --sum with no words or filter adds up every filed document.

```text
flib search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `QUERY` |  | `` | What you remember about the file (optional with filters). |
| `--category` | text, repeatable |  | Only this category, any case. Repeat it or use commas for any of several. |
| `--since` | text |  | Processed on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD, local time). |
| `--until` | text |  | Processed on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD, local time). |
| `--ext` | text, repeatable |  | Only this extension (pdf or .pdf). Repeat it or use commas for several. |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print JSON for other programs. |
| `--limit` | integer | `20` | Most results. |
| `--semantic / --no-semantic` | flag |  | Also find files by meaning, with embeddings (needs search.semantic.enabled); --no-semantic searches by words only. [default: search.semantic.default] |
| `--reindex` | flag |  | First embed every file whose vector is missing or stale (semantic search). |
| `--duplicates` | flag |  | Also list duplicates set aside in the duplicates folder. |
| `--issuer` | text |  | Only documents from this organisation (case, accents, Inc/Ltd... ignored). |
| `--kind` | text, repeatable |  | Only this kind of document: bill, receipt, invoice, statement, contract, payslip, tax, ticket, policy, report, form, letter, manual, other. Repeat it or use commas. |
| `--min-amount` | text |  | Only amounts of at least this much. |
| `--max-amount` | text |  | Only amounts of at most this much. |
| `--currency` | text |  | Only amounts in this currency (USD, BRL...). |
| `--due-before` | text |  | Only due before this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `--due-after` | text |  | Only due after this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `--period` | text |  | Only documents about this year or month (2026, 2026-09): the period they refer to, else their date. |
| `--sum` | flag |  | Add up the amounts of every match, per currency, instead of listing. |
| `--by` | text |  | With --sum: totals per issuer, per month, per year, per kind, per category. |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#search).


## flib due

List bills and other documents with a due date: overdue first, then the next 7 days.

Only due dates the AI read in a document count; nothing is guessed. By default the bills, invoices, statements and taxes (due.kinds) from 30 days ago to 7 days ahead that are not marked done (`flib fix PATH --done`), soonest first, with totals per currency. It only reads: no lock, and it works before the first run.

```text
flib due [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--within` | text |  | How far ahead: 7d, 2w, 1m (days, weeks, calendar months). [default: 7d] |
| `--overdue` | flag |  | Only what is past due, however long ago. |
| `--all` | flag |  | Also documents marked done, and due dates on kinds outside due.kinds. |
| `--issuer` | text |  | Only documents from this organisation (case, accents, Inc/Ltd... ignored). |
| `--kind` | text, repeatable |  | Only this kind of document: bill, receipt, invoice, statement, contract, payslip, tax, ticket, policy, report, form, letter, manual, other. Repeat it or use commas. |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print JSON for other programs. |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#what-is-due).


## flib fix

Correct a file's category or name; flib learns from it. `flib undo` reverts it.

--done marks a bill or other document with a due date as paid or done, so `flib due` leaves it out; --not-done opens it again. Both are journaled too: `flib undo` reverts them.

```text
flib fix [OPTIONS] FILE
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` |  |  | An organized file, by its current path. |
| `--category` | text |  | The category it belongs to. |
| `--name` | text |  | Its new file name; the extension is kept if left out. |
| `--done / --not-done` | flag |  | Mark a document with a due date paid or done (it leaves `flib due`), or open again. |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#teaching-it).

## flib reprocess

Reclassify organized files after the rules change (categories, hints, names, model).

Shows the estimated cost and asks before sending anything, then shows the plan and asks before moving. File names are kept unless --rename. Files you corrected keep your choice. It is one run: `flib undo` reverts all of it. A category renamed or removed in the configuration needs --rename-category or --remove-category first. --scrub-descriptions only cleans what the index already stores, without asking the AI. --apply-layout only moves files into their category's sub-folders. --fill-fields only records the structured fields of files filed before them.

```text
flib reprocess [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--category` | text, repeatable |  | Only files of this category. Repeat it or use commas for several. |
| `--since` | text |  | Only files processed on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `--until` | text |  | Only files processed on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `--ext` | text, repeatable |  | Only this extension (pdf or .pdf). Repeat it or use commas. |
| `--rename` | flag |  | Also rename files under the current naming rules (default: names are kept). |
| `--override-corrections` | flag |  | Reclassify files you corrected (flib fix) too; by default your choice stays. |
| `--rename-category` | two values |  | You renamed category OLD to NEW in the config: move its files over. |
| `--remove-category` | text |  | You removed category OLD from the config: reclassify its files. |
| `--to-review` | flag |  | With --remove-category: send its files to review, no AI. |
| `--scrub-descriptions` | flag |  | Replace phone numbers, e-mails and document numbers in the descriptions and tags already stored. Local only: no AI, no cost, nothing moves. |
| `--apply-layout` | flag |  | Move organized files into their category's layout (sub-folders by year, month or issuer) from what the index stores. No AI unless --ask-issuer. |
| `--ask-issuer` | flag |  | With --apply-layout: ask the AI for the issuer of files the index has none for (shows the cost and asks first); without it they stay. |
| `--fill-fields` | flag |  | Ask the AI only for the amount, dates, issuer, period and kind of files the index has none for (shows the cost and asks first). Nothing moves. |
| `--simulate` | flag |  | Classify (after asking: it may cost) and show the plan; move nothing. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Do not ask: send the files and apply the plan. |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#teaching-it).


## flib schedule

Run flib every day at a fixed time, or as files arrive (launchd agents), and check it can work.

```text
flib schedule [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--at` | text |  | Time of day, HH:MM (default: schedule.time). |
| `--mode` | text |  | daily, watch (run when something arrives) or both (default: schedule.mode). |
| `--status` | flag |  | Show the schedule and exit. |
| `--remove` | flag |  | Stop the daily run and watch mode. |
| `--refresh` | flag |  | Re-install the existing schedule as is (used after updates). |
| `--save-key / --no-save-key` | flag |  | Copy the API key from this shell's environment to the Keychain (default: ask). |
| `--check / --no-check` | flag |  | Test folder access as launchd will. |

More: [Getting started](getting-started.md#run-it-every-day).


## flib ui

Open the local interface in your browser: Status, Review, Search, Activity, Due and Settings.

A server on loopback only, for this Mac, under a random .localhost name of its own, so other servers on the Mac never get its cookie. The browser gets a one-time token through a file only you can read (`--no-browser` prints a link that works once instead). It ends after `ui.idle_minutes` without use, with End session, or with Ctrl-C. A second `flib ui` while one runs says so and exits.

```text
flib ui [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--open` | one of `status`, `review`, `search`, `activity`, `due`, `settings` | `status` | Page to open. |
| `--no-browser` | flag |  | Print the link without opening a browser. |
| `--port` | integer | `0` | Port on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 [default: a free one]. |

More: [Daily use](daily-use.md#the-interface).


## flib menu

Show flib in the menu bar: the cat's pose says what needs you, and its menu opens `flib ui` on the right page.

Built from tools that ship with macOS and started at login; nothing is downloaded. The menu shows counts only, never a file name. `--remove` takes it away again.

```text
flib menu [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--install` | flag |  | Install it and show it (what plain `flib menu` does). |
| `--remove` | flag |  | Take it out of the menu bar and uninstall it. |
| `--status` | flag |  | Say whether it is installed and running. |
| `--refresh` | flag |  | Rebuild it if an update needs it (install.sh). |

More: [Getting started](getting-started.md#the-menu-bar-item).


## flib inspect

Show what flib reads from a file before any AI is involved: hash, size, download origin.

With a configuration, also how much text a run would send and where it comes from (read from the file, or recognised by OCR on this Mac), never the text itself.

A file or folder that exists only in iCloud is reported as such, not hashed: reading it would download it. If the file is in flib's index, also show its status, category, why it is in review (if it is), and which name the AI judged better (original or its own) and why.

```text
flib inspect [OPTIONS] PATHS...
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PATHS...` |  |  | Files to inspect. |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print JSON. |

More: [Privacy and safety](privacy.md#what-flib-reads).

## flib eval

Measure classification quality on a built-in synthetic corpus of about 150 files.

The corpus is written to a temporary folder and run through the real pipeline in simulate mode with a throwaway database: your configuration, library, index and cache are never read, and nothing of yours moves. Before sending anything to a provider that is not local, it shows the estimated cost and asks. Reports category accuracy, the review rate, whether descriptive names were kept, and cost and speed. See docs/quality.md.

```text
flib eval [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | anthropic, claude-code, ollama, openai-compat or fake (offline). |
| `--model` | text |  | The model [default: the provider's default, as `flib init` picks]. |
| `--base-url` | text |  | openai-compat (required) or ollama: the API root. |
| `--language` | text | `en` | en or pt-BR: the categories and names to use. |
| `--limit` | integer |  | Only a fixed sample of this many items. |
| `--max-cost` | number | `1.0` | Stop sending once this much (US$) is spent. |
| `--vision` | flag |  | Send images and scanned PDFs to the model. |
| `--ocr / --no-ocr` | flag |  | Use the text recognised in images (recorded). |
| `--case` | text, repeatable |  | Only the items with this hard-case tag (e.g. image-text). |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print the result as JSON. |
| `--out` | path |  | Save the result as JSON here, for --compare. |
| `--compare` | path, repeatable |  | A saved result: compare this run with it. Twice: compare the two saved results, without running. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Do not ask before sending to a paid provider. |

More: [Providers](providers.md#measuring-quality).


## flib doctor

Write a diagnostics report for a bug report, with names, paths and secrets redacted.

It holds versions, the configuration (no API key, not even part of it), the schedule, database counts and the last run logs. Read it before you attach it.

```text
flib doctor [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--output / -o` | path |  | Write the report here [default: a new doctor-&lt;time&gt; file in flib's logs folder]. |
| `--stdout` | flag |  | Print the report instead of writing a file. |
| `--format` | text | `text` | text or markdown (paste-ready for a GitHub issue). |
| `--logs` | integer | `5` | How many recent run logs to include. |

More: [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#the-doctor-report).
